threads.body: The automated metadata collection does not currently run any `testExceptionSignalLogs` task: `.github/scripts/instrumentations.sh` lists only the ordinary/stable/experimental tasks, while those exception-event tests are separate Gradle tasks. Consequently the published instrumentation list cannot contain the exception events described here (the referenced generated PR contains only the default GenAI events). Add the relevant metadata-enabled tasks to the collection script, or narrow this documentation and feature scope.

threads.body: This aggregation again collapses records by event name and keeps whichever non-null severity is encountered first. `Files.list()` does not define iteration order, so if separate metadata files contain the same event name with different severities, the generated definition can vary between runs and omits one valid event shape. Aggregate by name plus severity (or retain a set of severities) instead.

Filtering performs another name-only merge and therefore discards distinct severities even if the file parser preserves them. Keep severity as part of the event identity (or preserve all severities) through this stage as well; otherwise the final catalog remains lossy and order-dependent.

Events are keyed only by name here, so the first observed severity wins and later valid severities are silently lost. This is not guaranteed to be fixed per name: the default `exception` event in `instrumentation-api/.../Instrumenter.java:346-359` is `ERROR` for server/consumer operations and `WARN` for client/producer operations, and modules such as Sofa RPC build both under one instrumentation scope. Preserve distinct `(name, severity)` shapes (or model all severities) so the generated metadata is accurate and independent of test order.
`File.createTempFile` is more conventional for creating temporary files. It ensures that each call gets a unique temp file. Guess this is fine too since the uuid collisions are improbable.
